- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” factor (e.g., reduce next 3–5 days’ forecast by 2–5% from peak).
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance by 15–25%.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add a “reversal buffer” to forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overfitting recent trends; use 18-day rolling average as a smoothing anchor for long-term bias correction.
